newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese man among survivors of Comoros jet crash.
newsitem.headline: Japanese man among survivors of Comoros jet crash.

text.p: Japan's Foreign Ministry said on Sunday that one of two Japanese on a hijacked Ethiopian airlines flight was among 54 survivors after the plane plunged into the sea off the Comoro Islands.
A Foreign Ministry official identified the survivor as Takahiko Sugiyama, a member of the Japan International Cooperation Agency and Japan's honorary consul general to the Comoro Islands.
"Mr Sugiyama suffered wounds to his legs. His life is in not in danger but his condition is not so great," said the official.

He said the Japanese ambassador to Kenya had left Nairobi and would soon arrive in the Comoro Islands to try to determine the fate of Nissan Diesel employee Hikoaki Nakauchi, who was also on board the ill-fated jet.
There were 175 people on board the Ethiopan airlines 767 when it ran out of fuel and went down near the Indian Ocean archipelago off the coast of Mozambique on Saturday.
